item.text: I’ve confirmed the repo is minimal and the target file is isolated. Next I’m reading `test/orders.js` directly so I can give a code-review style answer with exact line references.

**Findings**

1. [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:5) has an off-by-one loop bug in `calcTotal`.  
   The loop condition is `i <= items.length`, so the last iteration reads `items[items.length]`, which is `undefined`, then accesses `.price` and throws. As written, `calcTotal` fails for any input, including an empty array.

2. [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:17) `averageItemPrice` is likely computing the wrong thing for its name.  
   It divides the full order total (`price * qty`) by the number of distinct items, so an item with `qty: 10` heavily affects the result. If the intent is average unit price, this is incorrect; if the intent is average line total, the function name is misleading.

3. [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:18) `averageItemPrice` has no empty-array handling.  
   With `items.length === 0`, it divides by zero. In practice this is currently masked by the `calcTotal` crash, but once that is fixed it would still be a bug.

4. [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:23) `formatOrder` inherits the `calcTotal` failure, so formatting any order with items will also throw when computing the total.

Briefly, the module provides small order helpers: `calcTotal` sums `price * qty` across items, `applyDiscount` applies known percentage discount codes, `averageItemPrice` derives an average from the order items, and `formatOrder` renders the order as text with one line per item plus a final total.

Residual ambiguity: `averageItemPrice` needs a clear definition before fixing, because “average item price” could mean average unit price or average line-item total.
